If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and forecast is above 72.0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is below 70.5, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture lagged rebound potential.  
When sentiment drops below 0.0 after a peak, reduce forecast by 2.0–3.0% for the next 5 days to reflect bearish sentiment carryover.  
If sentiment is consistently 0.0 over 5+ days, reduce forecast by 1.0–1.5% for all horizons to reflect market stagnation.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3.0% in early horizon and sentiment is positive, reduce forecast by 2.0–3.0% for next 3 days to correct for sentiment-driven overreaction.
